title: Deploy Triage — Morning Digest (Apr 15 2027)
summary: Morning triage for private deployments: surfaced three customer blockers (networking, NTP drift, node GPU firmware), validated fallbacks for two customers, and assigned immediate actions for on-call and field engineers.
content:
Deploy Triage — Morning Digest
Date: 2027-04-15
Facilitator: Ava Martinez
Attendees: Ava Martinez, Liam Chen, Priya Kapoor, Diego Ramos, Ruth O'Neal, on-call: Samir Patel (SRE)
Purpose: Quick standup to collect overnight signals from field installs (VPC & on-prem), prioritize customer-impacting blockers, and assign owners for hotfixes / mitigations.

Highlights (top-of-mind)
- Three customer-impacting issues surfaced since last night roll: AtlasHealth (VPC) networking flapping, ClipperAI (on-prem) NTP/time skew causing KV cache misses, and BetaRetail (on-prem) intermittent GPU firmware panics on 2 nodes.
- Canary routing kept most traffic away from BetaRetail's affected pool; still seeing degraded tail latency for a small subset of requests.
- No new data exfiltration/security concerns; KMS health checks green.

Incident notes (chronological)
1) AtlasHealth — network flapping (JIRA-PDEP-3421)
- First alert 03:14 UTC: BGP session drop between customer AZ and our egress appliance after a router firmware update at their edge.
- Symptom: burst 503s and partial model load failures for sessions pinned to that site.
- Mitigation applied: traffic reroute to secondary peering point + temporary increase to request retries at the proxy layer.
- Action: Field SE Diego to coordinate with Atlas netops for rollback window; SRE Samir to capture packet-level pcap during next flapping window.
- Next steps deadline: 2027-04-15 18:00 UTC.

2) ClipperAI — NTP drift causing KV cache misses (JIRA-PDEP-3478)
- Observed by customer telemetry: 1–2s time jumps correlating with model state mismatch reports.
- Root cause hypothesis: embedded NTP client on management host occasionally pointing to a flaky NTP pool (customer-hosted).
- Temporary mitigation: bump tolerance for KV cache timestamp validation (config flag: runtime.kv.allow_time_jitter=true) — low-risk but adds a narrow window for stale KV reuse.
- Owner: Priya to test config in staging, Diego to schedule maintenance with ClipperAI for a controlled NTP fix.
- Risk note: prolonged jitter can cause subtle prompt-conditioning regressions — QA evals assigned.

3) BetaRetail — GPU firmware panics on two on-prem nodes
- Starts: 00:47 UTC; two nodes (node-12, node-15) in the customer's private cluster restarted after kernel oops linked to nv-host driver.
- Current state: node-12 repros on stress-run, node-15 stable after BIOS patch.
- Immediate mitigation: cordon node-12 and shift traffic to spare capacity; enable model-fallback routing for BetaRetail to a quantized variant to reduce GPU pressure.
- Owner: Liam coordinating with platform-engineering for hot firmware backport; Ruth to confirm spare pool scaling.
- Escalation: vendor ticket opened (NVDR-2027-88); ETA for vendor hotfix ~72 hours.

Ongoing smaller items
- Auditing of runbook gaps observed: need clearer checklist for NTP troubleshooting and for coordinated vendor escalation for firmware issues. (Action: Ava + Ruth to draft checklist by Apr 19.)
- Observability: missing per-node GPU telemetry at minute resolution for a few private clusters. Instrumentation ticket in backlog assigned to observability team (OBS-901).
- Post-deploy regression signal: one internal integration test showed higher decode latency vs baseline after the last runtime kernel change; SRE and serving-runtime to pair on a flamegraph pass.

Decisions made
- Short-term: enable runtime.kv.allow_time_jitter=true for ClipperAI as a stopgap (rollback on QA failure).
- Use model-fallback for BetaRetail (quantized model) until firmware backport lands.
- Delay non-urgent capacity scaling for BetaRetail until we get vendor's fix validated to avoid churn.

Action items (owner -> due)
- Diego Ramos -> 2027-04-15 18:00 UTC: Coordinate rollback window with AtlasHealth netops; collect router logs & pcap.
- Samir Patel (SRE) -> 2027-04-15 22:00 UTC: Attach pcap & interface metrics to JIRA-PDEP-3421; propose routing rule tweak.
- Priya Kapoor -> 2027-04-15 20:00 UTC: Validate KV-time-jitter flag in staging and run eval suite for prompt quality impact.
- Liam Chen -> 2027-04-17 08:00 UTC: Secure firmware backport plan with vendor and confirm list of affected kernels.
- Ruth O'Neal -> 2027-04-16 12:00 UTC: Confirm spare pool capacity and execute cordon for node-12; communicate expected latency impact to BetaRetail.
- Ava Martinez -> 2027-04-19: Draft runbook addenda for NTP troubleshooting + vendor escalation template.

Notes to self / loose threads
- Check if allowing KV time jitter could mask a clock-synchronization bug in the customer's infra; include a follow-up to require NTP health check in onboarding checklist.
- Revisit model-fallback thresholds in routing policy: current automatic fallback fires at 5% error rate, might be too aggressive for sensitive customers.
- Add discrete telemetry for BIOS/firmware version to onboarding checklist so we can detect at a glance if customers are running known-bad builds.

Communication plan
- Short incident notes to affected customers by 2027-04-15 21:00 UTC (Diego / Ruth).
- Internal postmortem outline to be prepared if any of the three incidents persists >24 hours (owner: Ava).

Meeting cadence / next check-in
- Follow-up sync at 2027-04-15 19:00 UTC (15m) to verify rollback/mitigation progress.
- Full morning triage continues daily at 03:00 UTC; consider moving to 02:00 UTC for a 1-hour overlap with APAC field engineers.

Appendix / refs
- Quick runbook refs: CONFLUENCE-Private-Deploy-Runbook-v2 (NTP, networking troubleshooting, GPU-firmware escalation steps)
- Related tickets: JIRA-PDEP-3421 (AtlasHealth net flaps), JIRA-PDEP-3478 (ClipperAI NTP), JIRA-PDEP-3502 (BetaRetail GPU panics)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-playbooks/pull/88 (kv jitter toggle test harness)

-- end of digest --

(Informal notes: flagged a couple of half-formed ideas for runbook automation — e.g., auto-collecting NTP drift histograms during onboarding; will sketch after triage)
